description:
The account-not-found path, and the only case in this folder that reaches FileStatus '23' at the ACCOUNT call site (gate G47): the cross reference resolves, and the account it names is absent from the seeded ACCTFILE. WHAT THIS CASE EXISTS TO PIN IS THE ORDER OF TWO MESSAGES THAT COME FROM TWO DIFFERENT PLACES, and getting it backwards is the likeliest way to break it. 3000-READ-ACCOUNT at app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl:241-250 takes its INVALID KEY phrase and displays 'INVALID ACCOUNT NUMBER FOUND' at :246 FIRST, from inside the paragraph, then moves 4 into WS-ACCT-READ-STATUS at :247; only after the PERFORM at :176 has returned does the mainline test that flag at :177 and display 'ACCOUNT ' ACCT-ID ' NOT FOUND' at :178 SECOND. Entry 7 of expectedMessages is :246 and entry 8 is :178, in that order, stated explicitly rather than left to intuition (practice B8). WHY ACCT-ID IS STILL POPULATED AT :178: :175 moved XREF-ACCT-ID into ACCT-ID before the read, and READ ... RECORD INTO ACCOUNT-RECORD does not disturb its receiving area when the INVALID KEY phrase runs, so ACCT-ID - bytes 1-11 of ACCOUNT-RECORD, PIC 9(11) per app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy - still holds the cross reference's own account id and renders as the eleven zero-padded digits 00000000007. The line is one DISPLAY of two literals around one operand and COBOL adds no separator of its own, so 'ACCOUNT ' + 00000000007 + ' NOT FOUND' is exactly 'ACCOUNT 00000000007 NOT FOUND' - the eleven-digit rendering follows from the PICTURE clause and not from a formatting choice, as does XREF-ACCT-ID's at bytes 26-36 of app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy (practice B11). HOW THE MISS IS MANUFACTURED: all fifty cross-referenced accounts are present in the full acctdata.txt, so the miss cannot come from the fixture as a whole and must not come from editing it. ACCTFILE is therefore seeded with a REDUCED SUBSET - acctdata.txt row 20 (zero-based 19), account 00000000020 - and acctdata.txt row 7, which is the row holding 00000000007, is DELIBERATELY OMITTED. app/data/ASCII is not modified in any way, because it is the only oracle this migration has (practice B3). Seeding one real row rather than an empty dataset is what makes this a genuine key miss against non-empty data rather than an end-of-file on an empty file, and the seeded row's first eleven bytes are 00000000020 - not 00000000007 - so the miss is guaranteed structurally and not by assertion. The other two seeds are dailytran.txt row 1 (zero-based 0), DALYTRAN-ID 0000000000683580, whose DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM at bytes 263-278 is 4859452612877065, and cardxref.txt row 21 (zero-based 20), which resolves that card to customer 000000007 and account 00000000007; that row is mandatory, because the whole point of the case is that the cross reference SUCCEEDS and the account read then fails. THREE LINES ARE THEREFORE ABSENT FROM THIS CASE, and their absence is deliberate: the INVALID KEY line of 2000-LOOKUP-XREF at :232 and the two-literal skip line the ELSE arm displays at :181-183, both of which belong to a cross reference that did NOT resolve; and the success line of 3000-READ-ACCOUNT at :249, whose NOT INVALID KEY arm is the one this case does not take. None of the three appears anywhere in this fixture - not as an expectation and not as a quoted phrase - so a reviewer's plain search for any of them over this file returns nothing, and each is cited by its source line instead (practice B11). THE POST-END-OF-FILE REPEAT, entries 9-14: the loop at :164-186 iterates once more, the READ at :203 reports '10' so :217 sets END-OF-DAILY-TRANS-FILE to 'Y', and the inner guard at :167 - which closes at :169 and covers ONLY the DISPLAY at :168 - suppresses the record echo while the statements at :170-172 and the account read at :173-179 sit outside it and run anyway, against the DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM the previous record left in WORKING-STORAGE. The stale card is the same card, so the whole hit-then-miss sequence repeats verbatim: entries 9-14 mirror entries 3-8 exactly, with NO record echo between entry 8 and entry 9. Fifteen lines in total. The repeat is asserted rather than trimmed, and hoisting those statements inside the guard makes this case fail, which is the point (practice B5). RETURN CODE 0, stated explicitly and never defaulted: an account miss is a normal, non-abending outcome. :247 moves 4 into WS-ACCT-READ-STATUS, which is a LOCAL FLAG the mainline reads at :177 and nothing else - CBTRN01C contains no MOVE statement targeting RETURN-CODE anywhere, and the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :473 is unreached, so 4 and 8 are both wrong answers here and 0 is the right one. expectedWrites is EMPTY as a positive assertion rather than an absence of interest: the program declares zero WRITE and zero REWRITE statements and opens all six of its files OPEN INPUT, and the six writes-channel dataset expectations below say the same thing per dataset at its exact copybook width - including CUSTFILE, CARDFILE and TRANFILE, which :158-160 open and :189-191 close but which no READ in this program ever touches, the only reads being DALYTRAN at :203, XREF-FILE at :229 and ACCOUNT-FILE at :243. The three seeded datasets are pinned unchanged on the final-state channel at their copybook widths - DALYTRAN 350 from CVTRA06Y, XREFFILE 50 from CVACT03Y and ACCTFILE 300 from CVACT01Y, whose FILLER X(178) is space-filled across bytes 123-300 and whose ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE keeps the copybook's own misspelling (I1) - which is what proves every FILLER span was emitted (gates G19 and G21); ACCTFILE additionally pins ACCT-ID by name at 00000000020 so the omission that produces the miss is legible in the expectation, not only in the seed. The cross-reference row is seeded at the 36 bytes the fixture actually holds and is NOT pre-padded; the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation supplies CVACT03Y's absent FILLER X(14) once, at seed time, and the final state pins all four spans by name - 16 + 9 + 11 + 14 = the whole 50 bytes, so no byte goes unasserted (gate G16, risk R-F). R1 and practice B4, documented and not 'fixed': the mandated class name TransactionPostingJob and the source header 'Post the records from daily transaction file' both promise posting, and the verified source posts nothing at all; CBTRN01C is also this migration's orphan, invoked by no EXEC PGM= in app/jcl or app/proc, so jobParameters is empty because there is no PARM for one to come from and the job carries no trigger (gate G13, requirement I4). Recorded for the same reason rather than reconciled by inventing a member: the in-code scenario of this ordinal in CBTRN01CParityTest reaches a different arm of the same READ by forcing a repository status, which a declarative case cannot express for a batch unit because a forced outcome is a screenRequest member and a BATCH_JOB case must not declare one - this fixture pins the seed-driven '23' that the model does express. BASELINE PROVENANCE, practice B12: these expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl :164-186 and :241-250 read statement by statement, cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts in app/cpy (CVTRA06Y 350, CVACT03Y 50, CVACT01Y 300, every offset mechanically diffable by eye) and against the real ASCII fixtures named above. They were NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, because executing it is empirically impossible in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed-file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, and no Language Environment CEE* services. AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers; the substitution changes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else, and is escalated for explicit user confirmation as risk R-A rather than silently absorbed. Bytes are US-ASCII, stated and never taken from the platform default, and nothing here reads a clock, draws an unpredictable value or consults the environment - CBTRN01C reads no clock, so the fingerprint is identical on every run (practices B7 and B8). review_rules returns exactly one line, "No user rules provided.", so no user rule governs this fixture; the binding standard is the enterprise-practice set, and its absence is not licence to assert less. Gates carried: G13, G15, G16, G18, G19, G21, G30 (the IF at :177 and the INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY arms of :243-250 in source order), G47 ('00' at the cross-reference site, '23' at the account site, '10' at the sequential read) and G51 (the tasklet body is driven directly, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP layer in the path). G32 does not apply: CBTRN01C contains zero GO TO statements.

THE READ SEQUENCE, DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED. expectedOperations names every read this run must issue, in order and with the key it is given, and it says three things no byte fingerprint can. First, WHICH VERB: the daily file's read is readNext because :203 reads sequentially and takes whatever record is next, while the cross reference and the account are read at :229 and :243 by a key the program built - a translation that turned either keyed read into a browse would produce identical SYSOUT. Second, HOW MANY: there is always one readNext more than there are records, because the loop at :164-186 reads again to learn it is at end of file, and the lookup that follows sits at :170-172 OUTSIDE the guard that closed at :169 - so the last lookup runs on the card number the previous record left in WORKING-STORAGE. Third, WITH WHAT: the key is recorded as declared, so on the trailing lookup it is the PREVIOUS record's card number, and on a run whose daily file was empty it is absent entirely because the record area never held anything. Every entry here was derived from this case's own expected DISPLAY lines - one echo per record at :168, one lookup block per iteration - and never from a run.
